create.title: New role
create.description: Create a custom role for this organization. Assign permissions afterwards.

permsSheet.title: Permissions — {{name}}
permsSheet.grantAction: Grant this permission to the role
permsSheet.revokeAction: Revoke this permission from the role

roles.description: RBAC roles scoped to this organization. Assign permissions per role; users get the union of permissions across all roles they hold.

permissions.description: The complete catalogue of permission keys you can grant to roles. These are global to the platform; bindings to roles live under each organization.

policies.description: Organization-wide security policy. Applies to every login, every session, every API call against this organization.

network.title: Network access
network.movedToRules: Which networks may sign in is set by IP rules, which every sign-in to this organization is checked against.

password.title: Password policy
password.description: Enforced at signup, password change, and password reset.

session.title: Session policy
session.description: Affects new sessions only; existing sessions keep their original lifetime.
session.maxAgeHelp: How long a session lasts after sign-in, however active it is. Also how long an application stays signed in. A duration such as 24h, 720h (30 days) or 2160h (90 days); between 1h and 8760h.
session.idleHelp: A session ends once it goes this long without being used. At least 15m and no longer than the maximum session age, such as 30m, 8h or 24h.
session.limitEvict: End their least recently used session
session.limitHelp: How many places one person may be signed in at once. A session ended this way can't be renewed; anything it already holds stops working within 10 minutes.

mfa.title: MFA enforcement
mfa.description: Who must use a second factor to sign in. Anyone who must and has none sets up an authenticator app before they get in.
mfa.optional: Optional — only people who set up a second factor are asked for it
mfa.required: Required — everyone uses a second factor to sign in
mfa.adminOnly: Admins only — anyone whose role can change anything (a write permission)
mfa.noteHelp: Applies to password sign-in. People an administrator marks as requiring MFA must use it whatever this is set to.
mfa.graceHelp: For this many days after you turn the requirement on, people who already have an account can skip setting up a second factor; they're asked each time they sign in. 0 means no grace period.

stepUp.title: Step-up for sensitive actions
stepUp.description: Before someone changes factors, keys, secrets, sign-in settings or other sensitive things, they confirm a second factor again. A confirmation counts only in the browser where it was made.
stepUp.windowHelp: How long a confirmation keeps sensitive actions unlocked in that browser. Signing out, a password change or a factor reset ends it sooner.
stepUp.methodsHelp: Only these confirm a sensitive action. People who hold none of them aren't asked to confirm changes to their own factors.

validation.maxSessions: Use a number from 1 to 1,000, or leave it empty for no limit.
validation.duration: Enter a duration, such as 24h or 30m.

resources.description: The protected resources RBAC permissions are scoped to. Derived from the permission catalogue — each resource exposes a set of actions you can grant to roles.

catalogue.title: Resource catalogue
catalogue.description: One row per resource, with the actions it exposes.
catalogue.empty: No permissions registered, so no resources to show.

check.deniedReason: No role grants this permission to this person in this organisation.

abac.title: Models
abac.description: Attribute policies, checked highest priority first. A matching deny always wins.
abac.emptyHint: Without one, roles and relationships decide every request.
abac.notFoundHint: It may have been deleted. Choose another from the list.
abac.needsAttribute: Pick an attribute for each condition to save.
abac.roleBlockTitle: The role block can't be saved yet
abac.relationBlockTitle: The relationship block can't be saved yet
abac.blockHint: Qeet ID saves attribute (ABAC) policies only. Remove the block to save this policy, or copy its JSON to keep it as it is.
abac.locked: Attribute policies are part of the Pro plan
abac.lockedHint: Upgrade to write policies on people's attributes, such as their department, network or the time of day.
abac.deleteDescriptionDeny: “{{name}}” stops refusing access at once. What it refused is then decided by roles, relationships and the other policies. This can't be undone.
abac.deleteDescriptionAllow: “{{name}}” stops granting access at once. Anyone it let in keeps access only if a role, a relationship or another policy allows it. This can't be undone.

errors.name: Enter a name.
errors.nameTaken: A policy already has this name.
errors.target: Enter a name, or * for any.
errors.locksOut: This deny would stop you changing policies
errors.locksOutHint: Nobody could then undo it. Narrow its condition so it doesn't match you, or limit it to other resources or actions.

unsaved.title: Discard your changes to this policy?
unsaved.description: They aren't saved. If you leave, the policy stays as it was.

authorizationAuditPage.everyAuthorizationChangeIs: Every authorization change is recorded in the hash-chained, append-only audit log.

authorizationSettingsPage.howTheAuthorizationEngine: How the authorization engine evaluates decisions, and where to configure related controls.
authorizationSettingsPage.theOrderAndSemantics: The order and semantics used to reach a decision.
authorizationSettingsPage.denyWinsDetail: An explicit deny from any matching policy overrides every allow.
authorizationSettingsPage.priorityOrderingDetail: ABAC policies evaluate in descending priority; default is deny.
authorizationSettingsPage.composedEnginesDetail: The unified PDP resolves RBAC (permissions) and ReBAC (relationships) together.
authorizationSettingsPage.explainabilityDetail: Every engine returns a grant-path / trace when explain is requested.
authorizationSettingsPage.securityPolicyDetail: IP allow/deny lists, session limits, and MFA enforcement.
authorizationSettingsPage.accessTesterDetail: Run an ad-hoc RBAC check with the full grant path.

reason.absentDeny: Denied by policy “{{name}}” (priority {{priority}}): an attribute it compares is absent.
reason.noAllow: No allow policy matched, so access is denied by default.
reason.conditionError: A condition in policy “{{name}}” couldn't be evaluated.
reason.explicitDenyUnnamed: Explicitly denied by an ABAC policy.
reason.absentDenyUnnamed: Denied by an ABAC policy: an attribute it compares is absent.
reason.conditionErrorUnnamed: A condition in an ABAC policy couldn't be evaluated.
reason.nothingAllows: Nothing allows this request, so it is denied by default.
reason.noTenant: There's no organisation to decide in, so the request is refused.
reason.engineError: An authorization engine failed, so the request was refused.
reason.unknown: The decision point gave a reason the console can't display.

trace.absentApplies: Policy “{{name}}” ({{effect}}, priority {{priority}}): an attribute the condition compares is absent → {{effect}}
trace.absentNotMatched: Policy “{{name}}” ({{effect}}, priority {{priority}}): an attribute the condition compares is absent → not matched
trace.conditionError: Policy “{{name}}”: a condition couldn't be evaluated → deny
trace.defaultDeny: No allow policy matched → default deny
trace.unknown: An evaluation step the console can't display

permissionsPage.thePlatformPermissionCatalogue: The platform permission catalogue, grouped by resource. Permissions use resource.action keys.
permissionsPage.wildcardWarning_one: {{count}} wildcard permission detected — wildcards grant broad access; prefer explicit keys.
permissionsPage.wildcardWarning_other: {{count}} wildcard permissions detected — wildcards grant broad access; prefer explicit keys.

policyTemplatesPage.startFromABattle: Start from a battle-tested pattern. Choosing a template pre-fills the Policy Builder with a real, editable policy.

policyVersionsPage.everyPolicyChangeIs: Every policy change is reconstructed from the audit log. History is read-only — server-side rollback is not available yet.
policyVersionsPage.theBackendRecordsEvery: The backend records every change but has no revert endpoint. For now, re-apply a prior state manually from the ABAC editor; rollback here is disabled.
policyVersionsPage.selectAPolicyTo: Select a policy to see its change history.
policyVersionsPage.selectAPolicyTo2: Select a policy to reconstruct its timeline.
policyVersionsPage.noChangesRecordedFor: No changes recorded for this policy

rbacPage.visualiseHowRolesGrant: Visualise how roles grant permissions. Click a role to expand its permission grants; drag to rearrange.
rbacPage.selectARole: Select a role to expand its grants
rbacPage.clickARoleNode: Click a role node to inspect the permissions it grants.

rolesPage.createRolesAndManage: Create roles and manage the permissions they grant. Role assignments propagate through groups automatically.
rolesPage.toggleAPermissionTo: Toggle a permission to grant or revoke it for this role.

conditionProblem.notReferenceable: “{{operator}}” can't compare with another attribute. Compare with a value instead.
conditionProblem.badReference: The attribute to compare with must be a subject., resource. or context. path.
conditionProblem.selfReference: A condition can't compare an attribute with itself.
conditionProblem.mixedEngines: This policy has a role or relationship block, which Qeet ID can't store. Remove the block to save it.

abacTest.savedHint: Checked against the saved, enabled policies.

rule.label: Policy

inspector.previewOnlyHint: It came from the template. Qeet ID stores attribute policies only, so remove the block to save the policy.

inspector.groupAllHint: Matches when every condition in it does.
inspector.groupAnyHint: Matches when at least one condition in it does.
inspector.attributeHint: subject., resource. or context., then its name
inspector.valueHint: true, false, a number or text
inspector.valuePatternHint: A regular expression; one that doesn't compile matches nothing
inspector.name: Name
inspector.effectAllowHint: An allow never opens Qeet ID's own admin: roles decide that.

answer.noReason: The decision point gave no reason.

trace.abacSkipped: No attribute policy can change this
trace.abacHidden: Attribute policies checked; you need policy.read to see which

trace.none: The decision point sent no trace.

person.title: Title
person.noUserRead: You need user.read to see who this is.

rebac.description: Who reaches an object through its relationships, and the groups and folders in between.
rebac.objectFormat: Type and name, such as document:readme.
rebac.objectsEmpty: Objects you open show here, with what they reach.
rebac.objectsNote: Qeet ID can't list every object yet: open one by name above.
rebac.openHint: Type an object's type and name above, such as document:readme, to see who reaches it.
rebac.emptyHint: Nothing names it yet. Add a relationship to start.
rebac.phoneNote_one: {{count}} person reaches {{object}} as {{relation}}. The graph needs a wider screen: they're listed under People.
rebac.phoneNote_other: {{count}} people reach {{object}} as {{relation}}. The graph needs a wider screen: they're listed under People.
rebac.selectHint: Select a node in the graph.
rebac.subject: Subject

rebac.noPeople: No one reaches it through this relation.
rebac.rootFacts: Tuples on it: {{tuples}}. People who reach it as {{relation}}: {{people}}.

addRelationship.description: Who holds which relation on an object. It counts the moment it's added.
addRelationship.objectHint: Type and name, such as document:readme
addRelationship.relationHint: One word, such as viewer, editor or owner. Relations don't imply each other.
addRelationship.subject: Subject
addRelationship.subjectHint: Everyone holding a relation on another object, such as group:engineering#member. It expands when access is checked.
addRelationship.bareHint: Without #relation this names the object itself, not its members, so no person gets access through it.

errors.relation: Enter one word, such as viewer.

testing.title: Testing
testing.description: Ask a question about access, for one person or many, and see what decides it.

asks.permission: Can this person use a permission? An attribute deny refuses first; then a role, or an attribute allow, grants it.
asks.relationship: Does this person hold a relation on an object? An attribute deny refuses first; a relationship, a role granting type:relation, or an attribute allow grants it.
asks.attributes: What do the attribute policies alone say? Only saved, enabled policies are checked, highest priority first, and a matching deny wins.
asks.authzen: The question your apps ask through AuthZEN: resource type permission asks for a permission, any other type for a relation on type:id.

testing.historyNote: Decisions from here and ABAC's tests, kept in this tab until you reload or sign out.
testing.historyEmpty: No decisions yet. Ask a question and its answer shows here.
testing.answerEmpty: Ask a question to see the answer, and the rule that decided it.
testing.pickPerson: Pick a person to see their roles and groups.
testing.noPolicyRead: You need policy.read to see the policies.
testing.noPoliciesFor: No enabled policy targets this request, so the attribute check alone refuses it.
testing.orderNote: Checked highest priority first; a matching deny wins over any allow.
testing.grantPathsHint: Each path grants the permission on its own.
testing.batchEmpty: Choose people and run, to see each one's answer.
testing.peopleHint: Up to {{cap}}, each checked on its own.
testing.userIdHint: You need user.read to choose by name.
testing.objectHint: Type and name, such as document:readme
testing.requestHint: subject, resource (type, id, attrs), action and context, as your app sends them.
